request: what actually is a vector?

beats.intent: An arrow v = (2, 1) from the origin of the grid
beats.narration: A vector is an arrow: here, two steps right and one step up from the origin.
beats.code:
stage.title("What is a vector?")
p = draw_plane(stage)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 1), label="v")
stage.caption("An arrow: a length and a direction")
stage.pause(2.5)

beats.intent: Two copies of the same arrow slid to other places on the grid
beats.narration: Slide the arrow anywhere without turning or stretching it, and it is still the same vector.
beats.code:
c1 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(-3, -2), p.c2p(-1, -1), color=YELLOW)
c2 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(1, -2.5), p.c2p(3, -1.5), color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("Same length, same direction: same vector")
stage.pause(2.5)

beats.intent: A red arrow w = (-1, 2) with the same length but a new direction
beats.narration: This red arrow is just as long, but it points another way, so it is a different vector.
beats.code:
w = draw_vector(stage, p, (-1, 2), color=RED, label="w")
stage.caption("Same length, new direction: a different vector")
stage.pause(2.5)

beats.intent: The two vectors written as columns of numbers
beats.narration: Each vector is recorded by how far it goes across and how far up.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"v = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad w = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", where="right")
pulse(stage, v)
stage.pause(2.5)

request: how do you work out the length of a vector

beats.intent: The vector (4, 3) on a grid
beats.narration: Take the vector that goes four across and three up.
beats.code:
stage.title("Length of a vector")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=5, y_extent=4)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (4, 3), label="v")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: Its across and up parts drawn as the legs of a right triangle
beats.narration: Its across part and its up part are the two legs of a right triangle, and the vector is the hypotenuse.
beats.code:
run = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(4, 0), color=GREEN)
rise = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(4, 0), p.c2p(4, 3), color=RED)
stage.label(run, "4", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)
stage.label(rise, "3", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)
stage.caption("Across 4, up 3: a right triangle")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: Pythagoras gives the hypotenuse: length 5
beats.narration: Pythagoras says the length squared is four squared plus three squared, which is twenty-five, so the length is five.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"|v| = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2}", r"|v| = \sqrt{25} = 5", where="right")
highlight(stage, v)
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The vector (-3, -4) with its own right triangle, also length 5
beats.narration: The same triangle works for any vector, even one pointing down and left: minus three and minus four square to nine and sixteen, so it is five long too.
beats.code:
u = draw_vector(stage, p, (-3, -4), color=TEAL)
run2 = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(-3, 0), color=GREEN)
rise2 = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(-3, 0), p.c2p(-3, -4), color=RED)
stage.caption("Signs vanish when squared: length 5 again")
stage.pause(2)

request: why does rotating a vector 90 degrees swap its coordinates and flip a sign

beats.intent: i-hat, j-hat and a yellow vector (2, 1) on the grid
beats.narration: Here are the two basis arrows and a yellow vector two across, one up.
beats.code:
stage.title("A quarter turn")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=3, y_extent=3)
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 1), label="v")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The whole grid turns a quarter turn counter-clockwise
beats.narration: Turn the plane a quarter turn. i-hat swings up to where j-hat was, and j-hat swings round to point left.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[0, -1], [1, 0]], riders=[i_hat, j_hat, v])
stage.caption("(2, 1) lands on (-1, 2)")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The rotation matrix sends (x, y) to (-y, x)
beats.narration: The old up-amount becomes the new across-amount, with a minus sign, and the old across-amount becomes the new up.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", r"(x, y) \mapsto (-y, x)", where="right")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: A second quarter turn points the vector the opposite way
beats.narration: Turn again: now the vector points exactly backwards, at minus two, minus one.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[0, -1], [1, 0]], riders=[i_hat, j_hat, v])
stage.caption("Two quarter turns: (x, y) becomes (-x, -y)")
stage.pause(2)

request: find the angle between two vectors with the dot product

beats.intent: Vectors v = (1, 2) and w = (3, 1) with the angle between them marked
beats.narration: Take v, one across and two up, and w, three across and one up. We want the angle theta between them.
beats.code:
stage.title("Angle from the dot product")
p = draw_plane(stage)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 2), color=YELLOW, label="v")
w = draw_vector(stage, p, (3, 1), color=BLUE, label="w")
arc = Angle(Line(p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(3, 1)), Line(p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(1, 2)), radius=0.8, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(arc))
stage.label(arc, r"\theta", direction=UR, color=GREEN)
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: v casts a shadow onto the line of w
beats.narration: Drop v straight down onto w's line. The dot product is the length of that shadow times the length of w.
beats.code:
av, aw, shadow = project_vector(stage, p, (1, 2), (3, 1))
stage.caption("Dot product = shadow length times |w|")
stage.pause(2)

beats.intent: The numbers: dot product 5, lengths root 5 and root 10, angle 45 degrees
beats.narration: Multiply matching parts and add: three plus two is five. Divide by the two lengths and the cosine is one over root two: forty-five degrees.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\cos\theta = \frac{v \cdot w}{|v|\,|w|}", r"\cos\theta = \frac{1 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 1}{\sqrt{5}\,\sqrt{10}}", r"\cos\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}", r"\theta = 45^\circ", where="right")
stage.pause(2)

request: why is the derivative of x^2 equal to 2x? i want the intuition

beats.intent: Two thin strips and a tiny corner added when the side grows by dx
beats.narration: Grow the side by a tiny dx. The new area is two thin strips, each x by dx, and a tiny corner.

r1 = Rectangle(width=0.35, height=2.4, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6).next_to(sq, RIGHT, buff=0)
r2 = Rectangle(width=2.4, height=0.35, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6).next_to(sq, UP, buff=0)
corner = Square(0.35, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.7).next_to(r1, UP, buff=0)

beats.intent: The algebra: the change in area over dx tends to 2x
